note: Saturday 10 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT. Weekend, markets closed -- this is a one-session increment over Friday's run, covering Friday 9 Oct's US close. Wall Street staged a broad risk-on rebound from Thursday's fear-driven selloff: S&P 500 7,811.54 (+0.59%), Nasdaq Composite 27,366.17 (+0.64%), Dow 51,654.95 (+0.83%), Russell 2000 2,806.98 (+0.46%), as VIX fell 3.70% to 14.84 from Thursday's 15.41 on easing oil prices and a tech-stock rebound ahead of next week's bank earnings; Real Estate (+1.85%) and Healthcare (+1.48%) led S&P sectors. Gold $4,220.30 (+1.52%) and Silver $61.11 (+3.46%) also rallied -- more a broad everything-rally than a fear signal. CNN's own Fear&Greed page remained hard to scrape directly; cross-checked mirrors (fearandgreedgraph.com, macromicro) put Friday's close at ~45, right at the Fear/Neutral boundary, up from Thursday's 38 (Fear) -- consistent with the VIX drop and index rebound. Crypto Fear&Greed eased further to 59 (Greed, per alternative.me) from Thursday's 64 as crypto consolidated. Breadth improved but stayed shallow: per TheStreet/StreetStats tracking, 52-week new lows still outnumber new highs (41 highs vs 120 lows, net -79, less negative than Thursday's roughly -300), only 291 of 503 S&P constituents (~58%) advanced on the day, and the % of S&P stocks above their 50-DMA jumped to ~36% from ~25% as the rally lifted laggards, while the % above the 200-DMA ticked up only slightly to ~46-47% -- the mega-cap/AI-concentration divergence hasn't closed. The weekly BofA Flow Show/EPFR print firmed up into a fuller, now-confirmed report for the week ended Wed 7 Oct (superseding Friday's preliminary approximations): a record $166.4B flooded into money-market funds (largest since April 2020; Hartnett: 'no rate cuts, no reduction in cash'), bonds added $33.8B, and global equities took in a net $12.4B as US equities (+$3.3B, first inflow in three weeks) and EM (+$2.1B, aided by China funds rebounding post-Golden-Week) attracted capital, Europe barely held an inflow (+$0.2B) and Japan logged its biggest outflow since May (-$3.3B); gold funds added another steady +$2.0B. CNN component-level detail below is reasoned forward from the headline index move, VIX and breadth (flagged as estimates) since a fresh official component breakdown for Friday could not be independently reproduced at filing time.

flows.period: week ending Wed Oct 7, 2026 (BofA Flow Show / EPFR Global, now confirmed -- a fuller report than Friday's preliminary approximations, superseding that file's guessed figures)
flows.narrative: The full BofA/EPFR weekly print landed with a much clearer and, in several cases, quite different picture than Friday's preliminary approximations. Headline: a record $166.4B flooded into money-market funds -- the largest weekly inflow since April 2020 -- with Hartnett framing it as structural cash-hoarding ('no rate cuts, no reduction in cash') rather than a classic flight-to-safety, since money funds already offer attractive yields. Bonds added $33.8B. Global equity funds still took in a net $12.4B even so: US equities swung back to a modest inflow (+$3.3B, first in three weeks), EM funds logged a second straight week of inflows (+$2.1B), helped by China-dedicated funds rebounding sharply as domestic investors returned from Golden Week, and Europe barely held positive (+$0.2B, second straight week). Japan was the standout loser, flipping to its biggest outflow since May (-$3.3B). Gold ETFs added a steady +$2.0B, continuing the record-setting 2026 run even as spot gold hit fresh highs Friday. Within US sectors, Technology funds took in $3.5B (largest in six weeks) while Financials saw their biggest outflow since March (-$3.0B).
